subject: Integration architecture & rate limits — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Hill <alex.hill@acmetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration architecture & rate limits — next steps

Thanks for the conversation this morning, Alex — great to meet you and learn more about Acme Tech's search/QA flow. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on architecture and rate limiting behavior before we loop in procurement: 

- Goals we heard: low-latency query-time reranking of top-K docs using embeddings + reranker, integration via SDK, and stable SLAs for production traffic (expected bursty peaks).
- Integration scope: SDK setup + auth, routing by region, structured output / tool-calling for action extraction, embeddings + reranker pipeline, and robust client-side retry semantics (429 handling, idempotency).

Clarifying Qs for you before Eng builds a draft config: 
1) Peak QPS / sustained QPS targets (per-region and global)?
2) Do you plan to handle dedup / idempotency in the client (X-Request-ID / idempotency-key) or do you want server-side dedupe windows for critical write operations?
3) For reranking: how many docs per query do you plan to score (e.g., top 100)? Will you store embeddings in your own vector DB and call Redwood for rerank only, or do you want Redwood to host embeddings?

Next steps I propose: 
- Can you confirm QPS and concurrency numbers (answer Q1–Q3 above)?
- I'll loop in Dev (cc'd) and Rishi to propose recommended rate-limit tiers, quota config, and a short SDK snippet showing exponential backoff + idempotency usage.
- Once we align, we'll include the config in the mutual action plan and pass to procurement for quota/commit sizing.

Attachments: integration-checklist.pdf (simple checklist), sdk-auth-guide.md (options: API key vs OAuth + recommended scopes).

Best,
Marissa

From: Alex Hill <alex.hill@acmetech.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration architecture & rate limits — next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Answers below: 

1) Traffic: we're expecting sustained ~150 QPS during business hours for the initial rollout (US region) with spikes up to ~350 QPS for short bursts (1–2 minutes) during peak events. Concurrency: roughly 200 concurrent active users.
2) Idempotency: for critical write operations (e.g., feedback, labeling), we'd like server-side idempotency support but will also send client-generated X-Request-ID values for tracing. For inference calls (read-only), we'll rely on retries in the client.
3) Reranking: we plan to store embeddings in our vector DB and call Redwood for reranking/scoring of top 100 results. We may want to experiment with having Redwood host embeddings later.

Also: procurement will want concrete quota tiers and an expected cost per 1M tokens for the rerank workflow. I can loop in procurement email (procurement@acmetech.com) once we have that.

One more thing — on retries: we'd prefer a retry strategy that avoids amplifying bursts (so jitter + backoff). Also need explicit guidance on headers we should expect in 429 responses (Retry-After, X-RateLimit-Reset, etc.).

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Search Platform | Acme Tech

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Hill <alex.hill@acmetech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T13:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Integration architecture & rate limits — next steps

Hi Marissa / Alex — quick technical proposal below. I'll follow up with a small repo of example snippets if you'd like.

1) Auth & SDK setup- We recommend API keys scoped to Acme's account for initial integration (rotatable keys via our Console / KMS integration). OAuth is available for agent-based flows but typically more complex for server-to-server rerank calls. SDKs (Python / JS) support passing an API key via the REDWOOD_API_KEY env var or as an Authorization: Bearer <key> header. We also add a X-Request-ID header for tracing.

2) Rate limiting & quotas- We can configure per-tenant (account) and per-route limits. For your numbers, suggested starting config:
  • Per-account sustained: 200 QPS
  • Per-account burst: 400 QPS (short window, auto-throttled)
  • Per-route (rerank): limit to 250 QPS to protect CPU-heavy ops
  • Request concurrency window and autoscale settings to handle short spikes
- Returned headers on throttling / normal responses:
  • X-RateLimit-Limit: total allowed in window (string seconds or requests)
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining: remaining tokens
  • X-RateLimit-Reset: epoch seconds when window resets
  • Retry-After: seconds to wait on 429
- 429 semantics: we return HTTP 429 with a structured JSON body {"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":<seconds>} and Retry-After header. We recommend clients always respect Retry-After when present.

3) Retries + backoff (client guidance)- Recommendation: full-jitter exponential backoff (see Jeremy Evans / AWS guidance). Parameters we use successfully:
  • initial_delay = 500 ms
  • multiplier = 2.0
  • max_delay = 8000 ms
  • max_retries = 5
  • Use full jitter: sleep = random_between(0, min(max_delay, initial * 2^attempt))
  • Backoff on idempotent read-like inference calls and on 5xx/429/network errors; do not automatically retry non-idempotent write operations unless an idempotency-key is provided.

Example pseudo-code (JS):

  async function requestWithBackoff(fn) {
    const maxRetries = 5;
    const base = 500; // ms
    for (let i = 0; i <= maxRetries; i++) {
      try {
        return await fn();
      } catch (err) {
        const shouldRetry = (isNetworkError(err) || err.status === 429 || err.status >= 500);
        if (!shouldRetry || i === maxRetries) throw err;
        const cap = Math.min(8000, base * Math.pow(2, i));
        const sleep = Math.random() * cap; // full jitter
        await delay(sleep);
      }
    }
  }

4) Idempotency / request IDs- For write/side-effecting operations (uploads, feedback, store), send an Idempotency-Key header (UUID v4) or X-Request-ID. Our servers will store recent idempotency keys for a configurable window (default 24 hours) and return 409 or the prior result if a duplicate exact request is seen within the window. For inference/read calls we recommend sending X-Request-ID for tracing but do not rely on server-side dedupe.

5) Embeddings / rerank pipeline- Calling Redwood for rerank only (you host embeddings) is fine. Send the candidate ids + context and we will return scores and optional structured fields. Recommend batching up to 100 candidates per rerank call and prefer using our streaming responses for progressive top-K updates if latency matters.

6) Operational notes- We expose per-route metrics in the Console (token usage, 429 rate, latency P50/P95). If you need a dedicated pool, Redwood Dedicated can provide reserved capacity and higher burst limits with SLA guarantees.

If this looks good I can: (a) drop a small SDK example repo with the backoff snippet and header wiring, (b) propose a mutual action plan with quota tiers and cost estimate.
